channel.title: ipe() Journal
channel.description: Notes from ipe(): music, design and how a small studio works. Written in English and Korean.

item.title: Calm by design — nothing here chases you
item.description: Nothing on ipe.rest is built to bring you back: no streaks, no badges, no pings. Why a studio for tired minds is designed to ask for so little.

item.title: Before the first note — a second of room tone
item.description: Every ipe() track opens on a second of room tone, the quiet sound of an empty room, before any music begins. Why we leave it in.

item.title: ipe. be still — the last breath of every track
item.description: Every ipe() track ends with one whispered line, “ipe. be still.” The rule behind that last breath: at the very end, quiet, and always in English.

item.title: Follow the journal, quietly
item.description: The ipe() journal now has an RSS feed: follow new entries in the reader of your choice, with no account and no sign-up.

item.title: We speak in code comments
item.description: Why ipe() writes its quietest lines as code comments: they do not run, they are not headlines, and they stay after everything else has finished.

item.title: Made with AI, and we say so
item.description: How ipe() makes its music: with AI (Suno), openly. Lyrics start as an AI draft that a person revises and reviews; the concept and the final decisions are ours.

item.title: late_night.lofi — the ride home
item.description: A series for the ride home after a late night — and its first single, “still compiling.” Slow lo-fi for the hour when the work is over and you are not home yet.

item.title: dear(you); vol.1 — ten letters
item.description: Ten ambient lo-fi tracks, ten letters, one feeling each — from empathy to peace. How dear(you); vol.1 is arranged, and why track 5 sits in the middle.

item.title: Why ipe() is named after an idle process
item.description: ipe() is short for “idle process” — the state a computer enters when it has no work left and simply rests. The story behind the name, the music, and the whispered “ipe. be still.”
